resale_co.name: Sale/Rental Certification (Residential and Mixed Uses)
resale_co.lead_time: Town recommends scheduling the inspection two weeks before the real estate closing; an extra fee applies if the inspection is needed in less than 10 days.
requirements: Water heaters, boilers, furnaces, HVAC and other electric or fuel-burning appliances in good working order, free of obvious hazards, with finalized permits
All open permits finalized before the certification is issued
Hot and cold water working in kitchens, bathrooms and laundry areas
Temperature/pressure relief valve discharge piped to within 6 inches of the floor and not threaded at the end
Main electrical service secured to the building with approved straps
Cover plates on all outlets, switches and junction boxes; no exposed wiring; installed GFCI outlets and breakers working
No open breaker slots in electrical panels; panels readily accessible
No extension cords used in place of permanent wiring
No open or partly exposed bulb incandescent fixtures in clothes closets
Handrails on all stairways and steps with four or more risers
Sump pump pits covered; sump pumps may not discharge into the sanitary sewer
Basement rooms used as bedrooms may need properly sized egress windows
Property must conform to all Town zoning and planning ordinances

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Sale/Rental Certification (Residential and Mixed Uses): check Sale of Property, give the new buyer, realtor and closing date, and sign. File it with the Construction Department with a check or money order. The website lists the office at the Town Hall Annex, 20 Centre Ave, First Floor (the form header still shows 1203 Paterson Plank Road, 4th Floor). Phone (201) 330-2027, Monday-Friday 9am-4pm.

resale_co.notes: Secaucus runs a Sale/Rental Certification inspection through the Construction Department for sales of one- and two-family homes, with a published fee schedule and a checklist aimed at real estate closings. The ordinance itself (ecode360) could not be opened, so the requirement rests on the Town application, checklist and department page. The fee schedule prints two expedited and two failed-inspection lines; the second pair ($30) follows the lead-based paint line and appears to apply to the lead paint inspection, while the first pair ($50, $37) applies to the certification inspection. Larger buildings: three family $145, four family $160, five family and above $160 plus $10 per unit; rental units $100. The live Town site showed a bot check during this session, so the forms and pages are cited from Internet Archive copies (original URLs: https://secaucusnj.gov/departments/construction and the /forms-documents/.../1369-... and 1370-... links). Carl Leppin's email is in the mailto link behind his name on the department page (decoded from the page HTML). A separate Certificate of Habitability ($50 first inspection) under Chapter 105 is for re-occupancy of units in residential complexes, not 1-2 family sales.

requirements: If the home is connected to a central monitoring system, show proof (company paperwork) that the alarm system is in proper working order
An adult must be at the home at the time of the inspection; inspections are between 9:30 AM and 2:30 PM

The Town form (updated 2018) still attaches the old state rule text requiring a 2A-10B:C portable fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, serviced and tagged within 12 months or with a recent purchase receipt; the state dropped the extinguisher in February 2025 and no newer Town form was found
Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarms (per the state rule text attached to the form)

fire_cert.notes: The Secaucus Fire Department is the local enforcing agency (registry code F) and its Bureau of Fire Prevention issues the resale smoke/CO certificate. Fees come from the form titled "Smoke Detector Inspection Request Form (updated 2018)", still linked on the June 2026 page; cited from the August 2025 archive copy because the live site showed a bot check (original URL in application_url). The form's text layer reads "fall" where the scan says "fail". The state directory gives the Fire Official's direct line as (201) 330-2059; the Town page gives (201) 330-2000 x 3170. His email is in the mailto link on the Town page and is also printed in the state directory. A separate Multiple Family Residential form ($100, $300 within 4 days) applies to units in multi-family buildings.
